claude delegate worktree.agent mcp: Racy: seen both matching and differing (8 pinned runs and the shards matched; a later shard run differed): the reference's task_status sometimes reads the task before its outbox finalizer records the result's context transfer, so its resultContextTransferId is null where Rust's is set, as in codex delegate's agent mcp.

claude delegate remote cancel.attempts: The cancelled task's result is steered into the parent's running Claude turn on both servers, and this fixture's CLI never reads it before its turn ends. The reference counts that steer delivered; Rust's resend_untaken_deliveries sends it again as a queued wake once the turn ends (a second run, its notification and message). A steering difference of its own, not of tasks in linked environments; the task, its result, its cancel and every call to the linked environment match.

claude delegate remote cancel.peer calls: Racy: seen both matching and differing: when its wait there ends, a server's follower reads the thread's reply only if the cancel has not recorded the task's result yet (the reference races the wait with the task's result, `raceFirst(endedHere)`), so either server may skip that one t3_thread_read.

claude delegate followup.live: Racy: the provider commit batch (#39502) decides by timing whether the first task's queued subagent updates commit together, and both sides vary: main's CI run 45294158798 saw the reference send one more subagent.updated after the task's context-transfer.created, and one of 8 pinned local rounds saw Rust send one more there. Matched in the other runs.
claude delegate followup.orchestration.subscribeThread (live turn: Racy: the reference's live turn sometimes does not settle before the harness stops waiting (the reference goes silent; Rust answers), seen both matching and differing, on main too.
claude delegate followup.agent mcp: Racy: in 1 of 8 pinned local rounds the reference's delivery turn did not settle before the harness stopped waiting (as its live turn sometimes does not, see the orchestration.subscribeThread entry), so its answer list lacks the turn's task_status. Matched in the other rounds.

claude delegate live.live: Racy: matched in 4 of 12 pinned local runs. Otherwise the reference steers the delegated result into the parent's running Claude turn (#39528) and queues the follow-up run while that turn still runs, sending the delivery's card once with its message and the queued run before the turn ends, where Rust also sends the card's pending and completed steer updates and creates the follow-up run after the turn ends. Which way it goes depends on whether the result arrives before the turn's last item.
claude delegate live.items: Racy: in 1 of 10 pinned local rounds Rust steered the delegated result into the parent's running Claude turn, so its notification item came before the turn's assistant message, where the reference queued it as the follow-up run after the turn. Same race as the live entry: which happens depends on whether the result arrives before the turn's last item. Matched in the other rounds.

codex delegate.agent mcp: Racy: on a blocking delegate_task wait, the reference's waitForTask races its outbox finalizer, so resultContextTransferId can already be populated on one server while still null on the other (seen both matching and differing).

codex thread tools.live: Racy: the reference's pull-request sync reactor reads a newly linked request on its own schedule, so in 1 of 10 pinned local runs its first link's synced and link-updated events landed a tool call earlier than Rust's. Matched in the other runs.
codex thread tools.agent mcp: Racy: since #197 Rust reads a newly linked pull request right after the link commits, apart from the tool call, so the agent's next list_thread_pull_requests can come before that read and show the link without its branches and draft state (seen both matching and differing).

grok agent mcp.live: Rust reports the provider thread's update just before the provider turn's start, where the reference's ACP adapter reports it just after (Rust's turn records hang from the thread record, which the thread's update creates). And the reference's provider commit batch (#39502) takes a Grok turn's first snapshots together (its worker runs only once the ACP stream has handed over what it read), so it sends the reasoning and assistant message items once, completed, where Rust, whose batch commits the first snapshot at once, also sends their running updates.
